ing: half thinly sliced for pickling, half in the broth
st: Rinse the brisket in cold water. Put it in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water, the half of the radish that is not for pickling, [[3 cloves]] garlic and the green onions.
Bring to a boil, skim off foam, then simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender.
Remove the beef and strain the broth. Season with [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar, then chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours until icy cold.
Slice the cooled beef thinly against the grain.
Toss the thin radish slices and cucumber slices separately with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt and let sit for 10 minutes.
Boil the noodles in a big pot of unsalted water for 2 to 3 minutes, or per package, until chewy.
Drain and rinse the noodles under cold running water, rubbing gently, then squeeze out water and divide into 4 bowls.
Ladle the cold broth over the noodles. Top with beef, pickled radish, cucumber, pear and egg.
Serve with [[2 tbsp]] vinegar and the mustard on the side so each person can season to taste.

ing: optional, cooked into paste with 0.5 cup water
st: Cut the cabbage into quarters through the core, then cut into 2-inch pieces.
Dissolve [[0.33 cup]] salt in [[4 cups]] water. Pour over the cabbage and toss, then let it soak for 1.5 hours, turning once.
Rinse the cabbage 3 times in cold water and drain well for 20 minutes.
If using rice flour, stir it into [[0.5 cup]] water in a small pot and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until thick. Let cool.
Mix the paste with [[0.25 cup]] chili flakes, [[6 cloves]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] ginger, [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce and [[1 tsp]] sugar.
Wearing gloves, mix the radish and green onions into the paste, then add the cabbage and massage until coated.
Pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing down, leaving 1 inch of space at the top.
Leave at room temperature for 1 to 2 days until slightly sour and bubbly, then refrigerate. It keeps for several weeks.
Soak the soy protein sheets in warm water for 20 minutes until soft, then squeeze dry.
Cut the sheets into rectangles about 3 by 4 inches and slice open one side to form a pocket.
Mix [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tbsp]] chili flakes, [[3 cloves]] garlic, half the green onion and [[1 tbsp]] sesame oil with [[1.5 cups]] water.
Simmer the pockets in this sauce in a wide pan over medium heat for 10 minutes so they absorb the flavor.
Lift the pockets out and let them cool slightly, keeping the sauce.
Stuff each pocket with about [[0.25 cup]] cooked rice, pressing it gently so it does not split.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and warm the stuffed pockets for 2 minutes per side.
Reduce the leftover sauce over high heat for 3 minutes until slightly thick, spoon over, and top with the rest of the green onion.
Rinse [[2 cups]] rice until the water runs clear, then cook it with [[2.5 cups]] water per your usual method until fluffy.
Put the chicken, [[3 cloves]] garlic and [[8 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked to 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken, strain the broth, and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
Return the broth to the pot with the mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season the broth with [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Mix the shredded chicken with [[1 tsp]] sesame oil.
Put a scoop of hot rice in each bowl and top with chicken, pancake slices and green onion.
Ladle the steaming broth over the rice and serve right away.
Soak [[1 cup]] mung beans in water for 4 hours, then drain well.
Blend the beans with [[0.5 cup]] water into a thick, slightly coarse batter.
Season the pork with [[2 cloves]] garlic, [[0.25 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and mix.
Stir the pork, [[1 cup]] kimchi, [[1 cup]] bean sprouts, green onion and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into the batter.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spoon [[0.33 cup]] batter into the pan and flatten into a 4-inch round. Fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, and the pork is cooked to 160°F (71°C).
Repeat with the remaining batter, adding oil as needed.
Mix [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and serve alongside the hot pancakes.

ing: or use cooked sliced beef or steamed fish
st: If using fresh fish, slice it into thin strips; if using cooked or steamed fish, flake it. Keep refrigerated.
Make the sauce by mixing [[3 tbsp]] chili flakes, [[3 cloves]] garlic, [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce and [[1 tbsp]] sesame oil.
Let the sauce rest for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water for 4 to 5 minutes, or per package, until chewy and translucent.
Drain and rinse under cold running water, rubbing to remove starch, then chill in ice water for 1 minute.
Drain very well and divide among 4 bowls.
Add the sauce to the noodles and toss with your hands or chopsticks.
Top with fish, cucumber, pear and egg, and sprinkle with [[1 tbsp]] sesame seeds. Add a splash of the ice water if the noodles are too thick.
Cut the tofu into 8 triangles or rectangles about 0.5 inch thick and pat very dry with paper towels.
Sprinkle the tofu with [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and cool 5 minutes, then cut a slit in each piece and gently open a pocket.
Mix [[1 tbsp]] chili flakes, [[2 cloves]] garlic, half the green onion, [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] sesame oil and [[2 tbsp]] water.
Stir about [[2 tbsp]] of this sauce into [[2 cups]] cooked rice.
Stuff each tofu pocket with about [[0.25 cup]] of seasoned rice.
Spoon the remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the green onion.

ing: finely chopped, salted and squeezed dry
st: Mix [[2.5 cups]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then stir in [[0.75 cup]] hot water until a shaggy dough forms. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and rest 30 minutes.
Toss the chopped cabbage with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, wait 10 minutes, then squeeze out all the liquid.
Mix the cabbage, pork, tofu, green onion, [[3 cloves]] garlic, [[1 tsp]] ginger, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sesame oil and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 3.5-inch rounds with a cup or cutter.
Place about [[1 tbsp]] filling in each round, wet the edge, fold over and pinch tightly shut.
Steam the dumplings in a lined steamer over boiling water for 15 minutes until the pork reaches 160°F (71°C), or boil them for 7 minutes until they float.
Serve hot with soy sauce and vinegar for dipping.
